frequency_question: How often do threatened sweeping unilateral tariffs against integrated partners actually get implemented on schedule rather than being averted by a deal or delay?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly announced, highly publicized unilateral tariff threats of 20% or greater on a major trading partner with a hard deadline. Excludes routine WTO dispute resolutions and antidumping/countervailing duties handled through administrative agencies.
coverage_note: 3 named; captures major high-stakes unilateral tariff brinkmanship episodes.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller bilateral disputes where threats were implicit rather than explicit executive declarations with firm deadlines.
skeleton: Threatened bilateral trade escalations involving major integration partners divided by resolution mechanism (negotiated settlement vs. implementation).
multiplier: 3 historical episodes enumerated with 1 hit and 2 misses.
validity_reason: Executive trade enforcement norms and the structural reliance on last-minute negotiated settlements remain consistent across recent presidential administrations.
